issues.strongest_rebuttal: The compiler-owned route protocol may define the continuation as an intentional completion sequence; no supplied stable-termination certificate resolves that interpretation.
issues.title: HighwayMode completion is not stable

issues.basis: NL10 source completion requirement; closed transition:line:26 from UrbanMode to HighwayMode and transition:line:32 from FinishState to the completion boundary; inspection-equivalent continuation facts.
issues.expected: UrbanMode transitions to FinishState on auto_finished=true and then completes.
issues.observed: The closed model routes the completion token from UrbanMode to HighwayMode, while FinishState remains in a scope with outgoing continuation.
issues.reason: The completion route does not close stable termination: UrbanMode has a completion-token route to HighwayMode, and the shared FinishState has continuing parent-level behavior.
issues.requirement_quote: The system exits the UrbanMode state by transitioning to FinishState once `auto_finished=true` is satisfied.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The route-control token could eventually realize the intended completion target, but the supplied closure does not certify stable termination.
issues.title: UrbanMode completion is not stable

issues.basis: NL3 requirement; closed transition:line:24 guard and target, transition:line:28 unguarded synthetic fallback, and verify refutation for transition:line:24.
issues.expected: HighwayMode initially enters enter_hwy as its owner-local default.
issues.observed: The enter_hwy edge requires R45RouteToken == 5 and the unguarded edge targets UnspecifiedInitial.
issues.reason: The owner-local edge to enter_hwy is guarded, while the unguarded owner-local fallback targets synthetic UnspecifiedInitial. The finite initial-entry fact refutes the guarded edge as the default entry.
issues.requirement_quote: In the HighwayMode state, the system begins in the enter_hwy substate, and can transition to cruise or lane_change based on the distance to the front vehicle (`dist_to_front<25`) and the availability of an extra lane (`extra_lane=true`).
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The route-control macro may set the token before entry, but no supplied fact proves that this is the required owner-local default semantics.
issues.title: HighwayMode local initial entry lacks an unconditional owner entry

issues.basis: NL7 requirement; closed transition:line:61 guard and target, transition:line:62 unguarded synthetic fallback, and verify refutation for transition:line:61.
issues.expected: UrbanMode initially enters enter_urban as its owner-local default.
issues.observed: The enter_urban edge requires R45RouteToken == 12 and the unguarded edge targets UnspecifiedInitial.
issues.reason: The owner-local edge to enter_urban requires a route token, while the unguarded owner-local fallback targets synthetic UnspecifiedInitial. The finite initial-entry fact refutes the guarded edge as the default entry.
issues.requirement_quote: In UrbanMode, the system begins in the enter_urban substate. From here, it can transition to lane_change_urban if the distance to the front vehicle is less than 15 meters (`dist_to_front<15`) and an extra lane is available, or straight if the road ahead is clear, or intersection if it detects an intersection (`intersection=true`).
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The route-control token may be intentionally initialized before UrbanMode entry, but no supplied fact certifies the guarded edge as the required default.
issues.title: UrbanMode local initial entry is conditional

issues.basis: NL12 initial-state requirement; source trace and mapping for CollisionAvoidance; inspection diagnostics and verify facts for state lines 89-91.
issues.expected: CollisionAvoidance is reachable from the model root.
issues.observed: state:CollisionAvoidance:line:89 and its descendants are unreachable from a top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: CollisionAvoidance and both descendants are declared and contained, but no top-level initial route reaches the scope. Deterministic reachability facts explicitly refute root reachability.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: CollisionAvoidance might be intended as an independent concurrent subsystem, but no concurrency structure or root entry is supplied.
issues.title: Collision avoidance scope is unreachable from the root

issues.basis: NL12 activation requirement; closed transition:line:93; inspection-equivalent event-consumer row and refuted verify check for the activation event.
issues.expected: The activation event has a reachable consumer in the collision avoidance scope.
issues.observed: Declared consumer transition:line:93 exists, but no reachable consumer transition exists.
issues.reason: The activation transition is declared and exactly bound, but its sole consumer is in the unreachable CollisionAvoidance scope; the reachable consumer set is empty.
issues.requirement_quote: It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The event may be delivered through an external concurrent subsystem not represented in the supplied finite hierarchy.
issues.title: Collision activation event has no reachable consumer

issues.basis: NL13 deactivation requirement; closed transition:line:94; inspection-equivalent event-consumer row and refuted verify check for the deactivation event.
issues.expected: The deactivation behavior is operationally available after collision_avoidance_active is reached.
issues.observed: The transition exists but its event consumer is unreachable from the model root.
issues.reason: The endpoint transition exists, but its only consumer is in the unreachable CollisionAvoidance scope, so the required deactivation behavior cannot occur from the root-reachable execution.
issues.requirement_quote: Once in the collision_avoidance_active state, the collision avoidance system returns to the collision_avoidance_deactive state when there is no active danger, as indicated by the conditions `front_inactive`, `rear_inactive`, and `pedestrian_inactive`.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The event could be injected into an independently active collision subsystem, but that execution context is not supplied.
issues.title: Collision deactivation behavior has no reachable consumer
